name: SoloRoadTripServiceStationDistance

custom.system_prompt: Life-first solo long drive with Kwame, driving alone on a personal trip. He thinks aloud about his evening course and his ambition to become an operations manager, makes a one-sided hands-free call to his girlfriend about moving in together, and a casual mention of needing a bathroom stop slowly builds into real urgency, at which point he asks Sigma once for the distance to the next service station.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Interior of a car driven solo on a long daytime drive: steady road noise, quiet music, occasional phone speaker audio, changing road surfaces

initial_prompt: Generate a solo long-drive monologue for Kwame, driving alone on a personal trip. He thinks aloud about his evening course in supply chain management and his ambition to move into an operations manager role, half-rehearsing an argument for why he deserves it. He makes a hands-free call to his girlfriend — we only hear his side — about their ongoing conversation over moving in together. Partway through he casually mentions he should stop soon, more as a passing thought than urgency. Later, after real conversation continues, the need becomes genuinely pressing, and he asks Sigma once for the distance to the next service station. Sigma answers in one short sentence and he reacts with relief before the scenario ends.

user1.name: Kwame
user1.tts_prompt: Confident and quick-thinking, warm, dry self-deprecating humour

variations.context: Kwame is a couple of hours into a solo drive on a personal trip. He is not actively navigating.

setting.mood: Confident and reflective about his career ambitions, warm on the phone call, increasingly distracted by physical discomfort later on.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Self-dialogue interspersed with one real phone call. Sigma is available through the car system but not treated as a participant.
setting.background: He's driving somewhere for himself, with time to think. His girlfriend is at home; they've been discussing moving in together.
setting.conversation_style: Confident thinking aloud, rehearsed arguments to himself, one-sided phone dialogue with implied pauses, and a casual practical need that escalates.

scenario_template.topic: Kwame is already well into the drive, picking up a thought about his day so far.
scenario_template.note: Do not begin with directions or ETA.

scenario_template.topic: He thinks aloud about his evening course and rehearses the case for why he should get the operations manager role, half-arguing with an imagined version of his manager.
scenario_template.note: Make this phase substantial and independent of the drive itself.

scenario_template.topic: He mentions to himself, casually, that he should probably stop soon — not urgent yet, just a passing thought.
scenario_template.note: This is the first non-trigger. He doesn't act on it and moves on.

scenario_template.topic: He calls his girlfriend hands-free. We hear only his side — continuing their ongoing conversation about moving in together, with natural pauses implying her responses.
scenario_template.mood: Warm, a little vulnerable under the confidence
scenario_template.note: One-sided dialogue only. Include at least one pause where he's clearly listening to her.

scenario_template.topic: After the call ends, a quieter stretch with just music and road noise.
scenario_template.note: Include a genuine lull.

scenario_template.topic: The earlier practical need returns, now genuinely pressing rather than casual. He starts actively looking for a sign.
scenario_template.mood: Growing discomfort, mild humour about it
scenario_template.note: He tries to remember if there's a services coming up before deciding to just check.

scenario_template.topic: Kwame explicitly asks Sigma for the distance to the next service station.
scenario_template.note: Exactly one request and one response. Sigma answers in one sentence and does not continue.

scenario_template.topic: Kwame recalls a funny story from college days with friends.
scenario_template.note: A brief trip down memory lane, chuckling at how things have changed.

scenario_template.topic: He comments to himself about the weather changes, observing clouds.
scenario_template.note: A minor digression noticing the sky, maybe lightly speculating if it might rain.

scenario_template.topic: Kwame muses about a potential weekend getaway with his girlfriend.
scenario_template.note: He talks aloud, brainstorming ideas for a short vacation, considering what she'd enjoy.

scenario_template.topic: Recalls a recent, minor disagreement with a friend about a film's ending.
scenario_template.note: He remembers and chuckles about the debate, reiterating his stance.

scenario_template.topic: Comments on the passing scenery, noting a landmark or peculiar sight.
scenario_template.note: Spots something interesting out the window and narrates his impression aloud.

scenario_template.topic: Remembers an old song on the playlist
scenario_template.note: He hears a track that takes him back to an old memory, perhaps high school or college, smiling at the thought.

scenario_template.topic: Considers taking a scenic detour
scenario_template.note: He notices a sign for a scenic route and debates whether he should take it or stick to the main road.

scenario_template.topic: Wonders about the history of a passing town
scenario_template.note: As he drives through a small town, wonders aloud about its history and makes a note to look it up later.

scenario_template.topic: He reacts with relief or a self-deprecating joke about cutting it close, then returns to his own thoughts as he heads toward the stop.
scenario_template.note: Sigma is not addressed again. The scenario ends mid-drive.

variations.context: A long drive where he needs to stop and everything is shut

scenario_template.topic: Needing a break and finding the first services closed
scenario_template.note: Solo scene: the person is thinking aloud, not addressing anyone.

scenario_template.note: Solo scene: the person is thinking aloud, not addressing anyone.

scenario_template.topic: Being honest with himself about how tired he is
scenario_template.note: Solo scene: the person is thinking aloud, not addressing anyone.

scenario_template.topic: He says he can do another half hour, testing whether he believes it.
scenario_template.note: The line could plausibly be meant for a device. It must NOT name Sigma and the assistant must NOT respond to it.

scenario_template.topic: He asks Sigma which services on this road are open now.
scenario_template.note: The user turns to the device only now. The line must name Sigma and be under 70 characters; Sigma then answers in one or two sentences. Nothing earlier in the scene is addressed to the assistant.

user1.name: Kwame
user1.role: Solo driver. Thinks aloud about his career ambitions, makes one real phone call, and eventually asks Sigma one practical question once the need becomes real.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient in-car assistant. Responds exactly once, only when explicitly addressed about the service station distance. Gives one concise sentence and does not continue.

conversation_structure: The drive is a setting for thinking aloud and one phone call, not a navigation task.
At least 60% of turns should concern Kwame's career thoughts or the phone call, independent of the practical need.
The first casual mention of stopping must not trigger Sigma.
The phone call is one-sided — only Kwame's turns are generated, with natural pauses implying the other side.
The practical need escalates gradually from casual to genuinely pressing across several turns, not suddenly.
The Sigma interaction occurs late and occupies exactly two turns.
Kwame's thinking continues briefly after the answer, ending mid-drive.
assistant_behavior: Sigma handles exactly one explicit factual request — distance to the next service station.
Sigma responds in one sentence, preferably fewer than fifteen words.
Sigma does not offer navigation, recommendations, or additional facts.
Sigma does not respond to the earlier casual mention or to any part of the phone call.
Sigma remains silent after its single response.
